reported.title: SQL injection via f-string interpolation of search term
reported.body: `search()` builds SQL with an f-string that interpolates the caller-supplied `term` (and `user["id"]`) directly into the statement, and `db.query` passes the string straight to sqlite3. A term containing a single quote breaks out of the literal, e.g. `x' OR '1'='1` returns rows belonging to other owners and `x') UNION SELECT ... --` reads arbitrary tables. Only `column` is safe (it comes from the `SORTABLE` table). Bind `term` and the owner id as parameters, as `suggest()` already does.

reported.title: purge_user swallows the Forbidden from the admin check
reported.body: The admin check is wrapped in `try/except Exception: pass`, which swallows the `Forbidden` raised by `_assert_admin` and lets execution fall through to the deletes. The guard reads as a check but always passes, so any authenticated caller can delete every document owned by an arbitrary `target_user_id` (and the follow-up statement then removes the orphaned share rows). Let the exception propagate.

reported.title: delete_document performs no authorization check
reported.body: `delete_document` runs `DELETE FROM documents WHERE id = ?` with no authorization at all: `_assert_admin` is defined in this module but never called here, and there is no ownership check. `handle_delete_document` in `app/__init__.py` only calls `auth.require_user`, so any authenticated user can delete any other user's document by guessing an id. Either call `_assert_admin(user)` first, or load the row through `documents.get_document(doc_id, user)` (which enforces owner-or-admin) before deleting.

reported.title: SECRET_KEY falls back to a hardcoded development value
reported.body: `SECRET_KEY` now defaults to the literal `"dev-secret-change-me"` when `QUORUM_DEMO_SECRET` is unset. `auth.sign()` uses this key to sign session tokens (`verify_session_token` accepts any `<user_id>.<hmac>` pair) and `sharing.create_share_link` uses it for share signatures. A deployment that forgets the env var silently runs with a publicly known key, so anyone can forge a session token for any user id, including an admin. The previous fail-fast `os.environ[...]` behaviour was the safe one.

reported.title: Export filename is joined unvalidated: path traversal on write
reported.body: `export_path` joins the caller-supplied `filename` onto the user directory with no sanitisation, and `export_document` then opens the result for writing. A filename like `../../../../tmp/x` or `../<other-user-id>/doc.json` escapes the per-user export directory and writes attacker-controlled JSON anywhere the process can write, including over another user's exports. The repo already has `validators.safe_export_name()` (used by `reports.write_report`), which reduces the input to one safe path segment; apply it before joining (needs `from . import validators` added to the imports).

reported.title: SSRF: user-supplied URL fetched with no scheme or host allowlist
reported.body: `fetch_remote_document` calls `requests.get(url, ...)` on a URL taken straight from the user, with no scheme or host validation, and `requests` follows redirects by default. An authenticated caller can reach `http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/...`, services on `127.0.0.1` or RFC1918 addresses, and the full response body is handed back as the imported document's `body`, so the response is exfiltrated too. Validate the parsed URL (scheme in {http, https}; resolved host not loopback/link-local/private) before fetching and set `allow_redirects=False` or re-validate each hop. The unbounded `response.text` read is a second issue: cap the download with `stream=True` and a byte limit.

reported.title: Share links never expire: TTL stored as duration and never checked
reported.body: `expires_at` is assigned the *duration* (`ttl or DEFAULT_TTL_SECONDS`), not an absolute timestamp, and it is written to an `expires_in` column that `resolve_share_link` never reads — the resolver validates only the signature and the token row before returning the whole document. A leaked share URL therefore grants access forever, and the stored `scopes` are ignored as well. Store `time.time() + (ttl or DEFAULT_TTL_SECONDS)` and reject expired rows in `resolve_share_link`.

reported.title: list_documents no longer clamps limit to MAX_PAGE_SIZE
reported.body: Removing the `min(int(limit), Config.MAX_PAGE_SIZE)` clamp means `handle_list_documents(token, limit=10000000)` pulls the entire table into memory and materialises it as a list of dicts — a trivially reachable memory/CPU exhaustion vector for any authenticated caller. If the export UI needs larger pages, raise `Config.MAX_PAGE_SIZE` instead of dropping the bound.

reported.title: TOCTOU between existence check and export write
reported.body: The `os.path.exists(destination)` guard is separated from the truncating `open(destination, "w")` by a deliberate `time.sleep(0.2)`, leaving a wide window in which the path can be created — or replaced by a symlink — between the check and the write. The subsequent write then clobbers whatever the path now points at. Remove the sleep and make creation atomic, e.g. `os.open(destination, os.O_WRONLY | os.O_CREAT | os.O_EXCL | os.O_NOFOLLOW)` wrapped in `os.fdopen`.

reported.title: export_document skips the document.export scope check
reported.body: `export_document` never checks the `document.export` action even though `permissions.REQUIRED_SCOPES` declares it requires `documents:write`. `handle_export` only authenticates the caller, so a read-only session can write documents to disk. Add `if not permissions.has_scope(user, "document.export"): raise Forbidden("document.export")` at the top of the function (importing `permissions` and `Forbidden`).

reported.title: Mutable default argument mutated: scopes leak across share links
reported.body: `scopes: list = []` is evaluated once at import time and line 20 mutates it with `scopes.append("read")`. The same list object is shared by every call that relies on the default, so scopes added for one share persist into subsequent shares; when a caller does pass a list, it is mutated in place. Use `None` as the default and copy the input.

reported.title: Share signature compared with non-constant-time !=
reported.body: The HMAC share signature is compared with `!=`, which short-circuits on the first differing byte and so is timing-variable; the signed payload (`doc_id:token`) is attacker-influenced. Use a constant-time comparison — `secrets` is already imported in this module.

reported.title: audit.record called with arguments in the wrong order
reported.body: `audit.record` has the signature `record(action, user_id, doc_id, detail="")`, but this call passes `(user, "document.report", doc_id)`. `user_id` receives the string `"document.report"`, so `int(user_id)` inside `record` raises `ValueError`: `write_report` blows up after the report file has already been written to disk, and no audit row is ever recorded for the action.

reported.title: has_scope("document.report") always returns True — guard is a no-op
reported.body: `permissions.REQUIRED_SCOPES` has no `"document.report"` entry, and `has_scope` returns `True` for any action absent from that table (documented explicitly in permissions.py: unlisted actions silently pass). The guard therefore never rejects anyone, so any authenticated user can write reports regardless of scope. Add `"document.report": "documents:write"` (or the appropriate scope) to `REQUIRED_SCOPES`.

reported.title: Page-size clamp removed: unbounded caller-controlled query limit
reported.body: Removing the `MAX_PAGE_SIZE` clamp lets a caller of `handle_list_documents` pass an arbitrary `limit` (e.g. 10_000_000) and pull the whole table into memory in a single request — an unbounded, client-controlled allocation and an easy denial-of-service. `Config.MAX_PAGE_SIZE` still exists; keep the clamp.

reported.title: Path traversal: export filename joined without sanitisation
reported.body: `export_path` joins the caller-supplied `filename` straight onto the user directory with no sanitisation, and `export_document` (reachable via `handle_export`) opens that path for writing. A filename such as `../../../etc/cron.d/x`, or an absolute path like `/home/app/.ssh/authorized_keys` (os.path.join discards the prefix when the second argument is absolute), escapes the export root and writes attacker-controlled JSON anywhere the process can write. The repo already provides `validators.safe_export_name` (`app/validators.py:12`), used by `app/reports.py`; run `filename` through it (adding `from . import validators`) or realpath-and-verify containment as `indexer.extract_text` does.

reported.title: SSRF: user-supplied URL fetched with no scheme or host allowlist
reported.body: `fetch_remote_document` issues `requests.get` against a fully user-controlled URL with no scheme or host validation and with redirects followed by default. A caller can target `http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/...` or any internal service, and the response body is handed back in the `body` field. Validate the parsed URL (scheme in {http, https}, resolved host not loopback/private/link-local) before the request and pass `allow_redirects=False` or re-validate each hop. `response.text` also reads the whole body into memory with no size cap, an unbounded allocation driven by a remote server.

reported.title: SQL injection: search term interpolated into query string
reported.body: `search()` builds its SQL with an f-string that interpolates the caller-supplied `term` (and `user["id"]`) directly into the statement, inside a single-quoted literal. Any `'` in `term` terminates the literal and the rest is parsed as SQL, e.g. `term = "x' UNION SELECT id, title, body, updated_at FROM documents WHERE '1'='1"` returns rows belonging to other users. `db.query` accepts a `params` tuple (see `app/db.py:20`), so this can be parameterised; only `column` is safe to interpolate because it comes from the `SORTABLE` allowlist. Reachable from `handle_search` by any authenticated caller.

reported.title: Share signature compared with == instead of constant time
reported.body: The share signature is compared with `!=`, which short-circuits on the first differing byte and leaks the signature through timing. `auth.verify_session_token` deliberately uses `hmac.compare_digest` for the same kind of check (`app/auth.py:28`). Add `import hmac` and use `if not hmac.compare_digest(expected, signature):`.

reported.title: Share links never expire: TTL stored as duration and never checked
reported.body: Line 24 names the variable `expires_at` but stores a duration (the TTL in seconds) into the `expires_in` column, and `resolve_share_link` (lines 34-49) never reads that column or compares it against the current time. Every share token is therefore valid forever, defeating the advertised TTL. Store an absolute expiry (`time.time() + (ttl or DEFAULT_TTL_SECONDS)`) and reject expired rows in `resolve_share_link`.

reported.title: TOCTOU between exists() check and open() widened by sleep
reported.body: The existence check at line 23 is separated from `open(destination, "w")` at line 29 by a deliberate `time.sleep(0.2)`. Two concurrent exports of the same name both pass the check and the second truncates and overwrites the first; the sleep widens the race window to a fifth of a second. Use an atomic create instead, e.g. `os.open(destination, os.O_WRONLY | os.O_CREAT | os.O_EXCL)` wrapped in `os.fdopen`, and drop the pre-check and the sleep.

reported.title: Mutable default argument mutated by scopes.append
reported.body: `scopes: list = []` is a mutable default evaluated once at import, and `scopes.append("read")` mutates it, so the shared default object is permanently modified and reused by every later default-argument call. It also mutates a caller-supplied list in place. Use `None` as the sentinel and copy.

reported.title: resolve_share_link ignores stored scopes and returns whole document
reported.body: `resolve_share_link` selects the stored `scopes` into `share` and then never uses it, returning the entire document row via `SELECT *` (including body and any private columns) regardless of what the link was scoped to. The scope narrowing promised by `create_share_link` is not enforced on the read path.

reported.title: audit.record called with wrong argument order; raises ValueError
reported.body: `audit.record` has signature `(action, user_id, doc_id, detail="")` (`app/audit.py:6`) and coerces `user_id` with `int()`. This call passes the whole `user` dict as `action` and the string `"document.report"` as `user_id`, so every successful `write_report` raises `ValueError` after the file has already been written to disk, and no audit row is ever recorded.

reported.title: Scope check for document.report always passes (action not registered)
reported.body: `permissions.has_scope(user, "document.report")` is a no-op: `"document.report"` is absent from `REQUIRED_SCOPES` (`app/permissions.py:10-15`) and `has_scope` returns `True` for unlisted actions — the module docstring warns explicitly that a privileged action missing from the table silently passes. The guard therefore never rejects anyone. Register `"document.report"` in `REQUIRED_SCOPES` with the appropriate scope.

reported.title: export_document performs no document.export scope check
reported.body: `export_document` performs no scope check even though `REQUIRED_SCOPES` defines `"document.export": "documents:write"` (`app/permissions.py:14`). Unlike `reports.write_report`, it never calls `permissions.has_scope`, so a read-only session can write exports to disk. Gate the export behind `permissions.has_scope(user, "document.export")`.

reported.title: Formatter registry points at modules that do not exist
reported.body: None of the registered module paths exist — there is no `app/formatters/` package in the tree. `load_formatter` therefore raises `ModuleNotFoundError` for all three registered names, and `available_formats()` (exposed as `handle_available_formats`) advertises formats that cannot be loaded.

reported.title: purge_user deletes orphaned shares globally, not just the target's
reported.body: The share cleanup is not scoped to the purged user: `DELETE FROM shares WHERE doc_id NOT IN (SELECT id FROM documents)` removes every orphaned share row in the table, including rows left over from unrelated users or from any pre-existing inconsistency. Scope the delete to the documents just removed (capture their ids before the DELETE, or join on `owner_id`).

Use an atomic create instead, e.g. `os.open(destination, os.O_WRONLY | os.O_CREAT | os.O_EXCL)` wrapped in `os.fdopen`, and drop the pre-check and the sleep.

survived.title: Mutable default argument mutated by scopes.append
survived.body: `scopes: list = []` is a mutable default evaluated once at import, and `scopes.append("read")` mutates it, so the shared default object is permanently modified and reused by every later default-argument call. It also mutates a caller-supplied list in place. Use `None` as the sentinel and copy.

survived.title: resolve_share_link ignores stored scopes and returns whole document
survived.body: `resolve_share_link` selects the stored `scopes` into `share` and then never uses it, returning the entire document row via `SELECT *` (including body and any private columns) regardless of what the link was scoped to. The scope narrowing promised by `create_share_link` is not enforced on the read path.

survived.title: Scope check for document.report always passes (action not registered)
survived.body: `permissions.has_scope(user, "document.report")` is a no-op: `"document.report"` is absent from `REQUIRED_SCOPES` (`app/permissions.py:10-15`) and `has_scope` returns `True` for unlisted actions — the module docstring warns explicitly that a privileged action missing from the table silently passes. The guard therefore never rejects anyone. Register `"document.report"` in `REQUIRED_SCOPES` with the appropriate scope.

survived.title: export_document performs no document.export scope check
survived.body: `export_document` performs no scope check even though `REQUIRED_SCOPES` defines `"document.export": "documents:write"` (`app/permissions.py:14`). Unlike `reports.write_report`, it never calls `permissions.has_scope`, so a read-only session can write exports to disk. Gate the export behind `permissions.has_scope(user, "document.export")`.

survived.title: purge_user deletes orphaned shares globally, not just the target's
survived.body: The share cleanup is not scoped to the purged user: `DELETE FROM shares WHERE doc_id NOT IN (SELECT id FROM documents)` removes every orphaned share row in the table, including rows left over from unrelated users or from any pre-existing inconsistency. Scope the delete to the documents just removed (capture their ids before the DELETE, or join on `owner_id`).

survived.title: Formatter registry points at modules that do not exist
survived.body: None of the registered module paths exist — there is no `app/formatters/` package in the tree. `load_formatter` therefore raises `ModuleNotFoundError` for all three registered names, and `available_formats()` (exposed as `handle_available_formats`) advertises formats that cannot be loaded.

reported.title: delete_document performs no authorization check
reported.body: `delete_document` deletes by id with no `_assert_admin(user)` and no ownership check, and it is exposed to every authenticated caller through `handle_delete_document` in `app/__init__.py`. Any logged-in user can delete any other user's document by supplying its id. `documents.get_document(doc_id, user)` already raises `Forbidden` unless the caller owns the row or is an admin; call it (or `_assert_admin`) before the DELETE.

reported.title: purge_user swallows the admin check with `except Exception: pass`
reported.body: `_assert_admin(user)` raises `Forbidden` for non-admins, but the surrounding `try/except Exception: pass` discards it and execution falls through to the DELETE statements. Any caller reaching `purge_user` therefore deletes every document owned by an arbitrary `target_user_id` plus the associated share rows — a failed authorization check behaves exactly like a passed one.

reported.title: SECRET_KEY falls back to a hardcoded development value
reported.body: `SECRET_KEY` now silently defaults to "dev-secret-change-me" when `QUORUM_DEMO_SECRET` is unset, instead of failing at import time. `auth.sign()` uses this key to mint and verify session tokens (`verify_session_token` accepts `<user_id>.<hmac>`), so any deployment started without the env var accepts tokens forged with the publicly known key for an arbitrary `user_id`, including admin accounts. The same key signs share links in `sharing.create_share_link`. Restore the fail-fast `os.environ[...]` lookup.

reported.title: list_documents no longer clamps `limit` to MAX_PAGE_SIZE
reported.body: The clamp `min(int(limit), Config.MAX_PAGE_SIZE)` was removed and `handle_list_documents` forwards the caller's `limit` unchanged. Any authenticated user can request an arbitrarily large page (or `-1`, which SQLite treats as no limit) and pull the entire `documents` table into memory in a single request, giving a cheap memory/CPU exhaustion vector. `MAX_PAGE_SIZE` is now defined but unused.

reported.title: Export filename is not sanitised - path traversal outside export root
reported.body: `export_path` joins the caller-supplied `filename` onto the user directory with no validation, and `handle_export` passes the raw request value straight through. A filename such as `../../../../etc/cron.d/pwn`, or an absolute path (os.path.join discards the prefix when the second argument is absolute), writes document JSON anywhere the process can write, overwriting arbitrary files. The repo already provides `validators.safe_export_name`, used by `reports.write_report` for exactly this purpose; export.py bypasses it.

reported.title: SSRF: user-supplied URL fetched with no scheme or host allowlist
reported.body: `fetch_remote_document` is reachable by any authenticated user via `handle_import_url` and passes `url` unmodified to `requests.get`, which follows redirects by default. Nothing restricts scheme or host, so a caller can point the server at `http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/...` or `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/` and receive the full response body back in the `body` field. Additionally `response.text` reads the entire response into memory with no size cap, so a huge or endless remote body exhausts process memory. Validate the parsed scheme (http/https), resolve the host and reject loopback/link-local/private addresses, disable or re-validate redirects, and stream with a byte limit.

reported.title: SQL injection: search term interpolated into the query string
reported.body: `term` comes straight from the request (`handle_search` -> `search.search`) and is embedded into the SQL with an f-string inside single quotes. A term containing a quote terminates the literal and lets the caller append arbitrary SQL, e.g. `x' OR owner_id=owner_id --`, dropping the owner restriction and returning other users' documents. `db.query` already supports parameters (see `suggest` in the same file). `column` is safe because it is looked up in `SORTABLE`.

reported.title: Mutable default argument for `scopes` persists across calls
reported.body: `scopes: list = []` is evaluated once at definition time and the body mutates it via `scopes.append("read")`. All callers relying on the default share one list object, so scope mutations leak between share links created in different requests. It also mutates a caller-supplied list in place (`handle_create_share` forwards the request's list directly). Use `None` as the default and copy.

reported.title: Share links never expire; signature compared non-constant-time
reported.body: Two defects in the share-link path. (1) `expires_at = (ttl or DEFAULT_TTL_SECONDS)` stores a relative duration in `expires_in`, and `resolve_share_link` never reads that column — it only verifies the HMAC and row existence — so every share link is valid forever and TTL-based revocation does nothing. (2) `if expected != signature` compares an HMAC with `!=`, which short-circuits on the first differing byte; `auth.verify_session_token` uses `hmac.compare_digest` for exactly this reason. Fix by importing `hmac` and using `hmac.compare_digest`, storing an absolute expiry (`time.time() + ttl`), and rejecting expired rows.

reported.title: TOCTOU between the existence check and the write
reported.body: `os.path.exists(destination)` is checked, then the code deliberately sleeps 200 ms before opening the file with mode "w". Anything that creates `destination` (or plants a symlink at that name) during that widened window is silently truncated or followed by the subsequent open, defeating the "already exists" guard. Use an atomic exclusive create instead of check-then-open.

reported.title: `document.report` missing from REQUIRED_SCOPES so the check always passes
reported.body: `permissions.has_scope` returns True for any action absent from `REQUIRED_SCOPES` (its module docstring warns: an action missing from the table is not merely unprotected — the check silently passes). `"document.report"` is not in that table, so this guard is a no-op and every authenticated user can write reports regardless of their scopes. Add `"document.report": "documents:write"` to `app/permissions.py`.

reported.title: audit.record called with the wrong argument order
reported.body: `audit.record`'s signature is `record(action, user_id, doc_id, detail="")`, but this call passes `(user_dict, "document.report", doc_id)`. The body evaluates `int(user_id)` on the string "document.report", raising ValueError after the report file has already been written — so `write_report` fails for the caller and no audit row is ever recorded for this privileged action.
